questions.question: List four effects that a force can have on an object, with an everyday example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Start motion (kicking a ball from rest); speed up (pedalling harder); slow down or stop (braking a bicycle); change direction (bat hitting a ball); change shape (squashing a can). Any four.

questions.question: State the principle that forces act in pairs and use it to explain how a swimmer moves forward.
questions.expected_answer: When A exerts a force on B, B exerts an equal and opposite force on A. The swimmer pushes the water backwards, so the water pushes the swimmer forwards with an equal force.

questions.question: Explain why the weight of a book on a table and the push of the table on the book are not a force pair.
questions.expected_answer: Both forces act on the same object (the book) and are different types (gravitational and contact). The partner of the book's weight is the book pulling the Earth upwards; the partner of the table's push is the book pushing down on the table.
